hero.subtitle: From backups on I-5 to fender-benders along Avenida Pico, San Clemente's weekend traffic can turn serious fast. We'll connect you with an independent attorney who can help you sort out what comes next.

about.title: San Clemente Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Clemente's stretch of I-5, along with Avenida Pico, S El Camino Real, and N El Camino Real, sees a steady flow of local and through traffic, and public records show 182 injury collisions and 240 injured people in the most recent year, with a pattern of higher activity on Saturday afternoons. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the period right after matters — insurance adjusters often call quickly, hoping to lock in a recorded statement before you've spoken with anyone else. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured San Clemente residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney working on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. We don't practice law ourselves; we simply make the introduction so you can get informed guidance about medical documentation, evidence preservation, and your options under California law while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, though claims against a government entity (like a city road issue) can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can help make sure that deadline doesn't slip by unnoticed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible, you can still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. Insurers know this and may try to shift blame onto you early — before you've had counsel review the police report or corridor camera footage.

items.title: No Cap Means Careful Documentation Matters
items.desc: California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, but that only helps if your injuries and losses are properly documented. An independent attorney can help you avoid giving a recorded statement that later gets used to minimize your claim.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on I-5 near San Clemente — do I still have a claim if I was partly at fault?
items.answer: Likely yes. California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to recover damages even if you share some blame, though your recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement — should I give one?
items.answer: It's worth pausing before you do. Recorded statements are often used by insurers to find inconsistencies or minimize your claim later, and you're generally not obligated to provide one right away. Speaking with an independent attorney first can help you understand your rights before you respond.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a San Clemente car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your crash involved a government entity, such as a road maintained by the city or county, the notice deadline can be much shorter, sometimes six months, so it's best not to wait to get guidance.
